newsitem.title: IRAQ: Chronology of Iraqi confrontation with the West.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of Iraqi confrontation with the West.

text.p: The following is a chronology of main events in Iraq's confrontation with the United States since the end of the 1991 Gulf War.

February 1991 - U.S. and allied forces cease fire after driving Iraqi forces from Kuwait. Iraq tells army to stop fighting. Later in the year U.S., British and French planes start patrolling Iraqi skies to shield Iraq's Kurds from attack by Baghdad.
December 1992 - U.S. F-16 fighter shoots down an Iraqi MiG in the no-fly zone in southern Iraq.
January 1993 - Some 110 U.S. and allied planes blast Iraqi missile sites in the no-fly zone in retaliation for violations of ceasefire terms. Iraq says 19 killed in attack.

June 1993 - U.S. warships fire 23 cruise missiles at Baghdad, destroying Iraqi intelligence service headquarters wing. Missiles kill six people. Attack ordered to avenge Iraqi plot to kill former U.S. president George Bush.
July and August 1993 - U.S. planes strike anti-aircraft missile sites in series of missile attacks in no-fly zone over southern and northern Iraq.
October 1994 - Iraqi Republican Guards move into southern Iraq near border with Kuwait. United States and Britain send forces towards Kuwait to counter buildup.

Aug 31, 1996 - President Bill Clinton places U.S. forces in the Gulf on alert after Iraqi troops supporting Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) attack and capture northern Iraqi city of Arbil from rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK).
Sept 3, 1996 - U.S. forces fire 27 sea- and air-launched missiles at targets in southern Iraq. The U.S. says strikes are warning to Iraq to comply with Gulf War ceasefire resolutions.
